newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico interest rates touch new ceiling, says bank.
newsitem.headline: Mexico interest rates touch new ceiling, says bank.

text.p: Mexico's interest rates have reached a new ceiling, and could resume their downward trend, bank Ixe said in a report released Sunday.

"We consider that interest rates have touched a new ceiling and could return to the downward trend in the next sessions, although this will be a more gradual decline than in the first few weeks of the year," it said.
The Mexican bank said worries over the economic and financial fallout of the fight in the U.S. over whether to certify Mexico as a trustworthy ally in the fight against drugs had been exaggerated.

The U.S. House of Representatives voted last week to overturn President Bill Clinton's "certification" of Mexico on March 1 unless certain conditions are met. The Clinton administration has promised to veto the House resolution if need be.
One-month Cetes rates have risen 458-basis-points in the last two auctions, mainly on the political worries and fears of rising interest rates in the U.S.

"In this sense, the size of the increase in short-term interest rates was exaggerated, especially since the decline in monthly inflation from February to March does not justify the actual interest rate levels," Ixe said.
At the primary auction last Tuesday, the one-month paper rate rose a sharp 201 basis points to yield 23.17 percent.
Rates fell for 10 straight weeks before rising at the last two auctions. The decline had sent rates to their lowest levels since the 1994 peso crash.
